label: Review becomes verification
title: From reading code to verifying evidence
thesis: As AI-generated changes exceed the capacity for line-by-line human review, software assurance shifts from inspecting code towards verifying intended behaviour, test evidence, security properties and architectural constraints. Automated systems take over routine checking, while human attention concentrates on intent, high-risk decisions, exceptions and accountability.
currentPressure: Generation capacity is growing faster than review capacity, producing longer queues and lower acceptance rates for AI-authored changes.

implications.statement: Reviewing shifts from reading diffs to judging whether the evidence accompanying a change is sufficient.
Specifying acceptance criteria and interpreting verification output become more valuable than close reading of code.
Accountability for defects moves from the author of a change toward whoever accepted the evidence for it.

evidence.note: 4.6x longer review waits — establishes the pressure, not the shift
AI PRs accepted 32.7% vs 84.4% — pressure only
synthesis of other reports on review time
routine checking automated ahead of humans
review agents without humans: 45% vs 68% merge rate, most feedback noise
a practitioner reporting his own shift from reading diffs to checking machine-produced evidence
review named as the most leveraged engineering skill — direction of pressure, not evidence of the shift
telemetry from 22,000 developers: the constraint has moved past throughput

Shipped release that moves per-action approval to automated evaluation: safe operations proceed immediately, ambiguous or high-risk ones route to a human. The reviewer becomes an exception handler by product design.

Survey of 820 technology professionals: 55% of QA teams report their focus moving from executing tests to quality analytics, while 77% express confidence in AI output and only 39% have fully automated audit trails.

52 practitioners running a Builder/Reviewer workflow on real legacy tasks, in which a model critiques artifacts before human review and humans hold explicit approval gates between phases; ~83% report less rework.

200 security practitioners: 62% say keeping up with the volume of code requiring security review is getting harder, and 66% spend over half their time validating findings rather than fixing. Measures assurance capacity under strain; shows no direction on how assurance is performed.

reachRationale: Automated first-pass review is running in production at several unrelated organisations and tooling vendors are building for it, but assurance practice outside those forerunners is still diff-centric.
whatWouldChangeThis: Review practice stays diff-centric through 2027 despite sustained volume growth
Automated reviewers are rolled back after escaped-defect rates rise
